title: Fragment coalescer: prefill-prioritized bucketing and decode interleave
creator: Marco Perez
description:
Goal: Reduce wasted padding and improve kernel utilization by dynamically coalescing short sequences into fragment groups that are scheduled with prefill-priority and decode-interleaving. This ticket implements a runtime component (Fragment Coalescer) that: 1) observes incoming request length distribution and kernel throughput profiles; 2) maintains short-lived "fragments" (virtual concatenations of short requests) with affinity hints for attention kernels and KV cache boundaries; 3) schedules prefill and decode so fragments are packed for high-throughput kernels while preserving per-request latency SLOs through decode interleaving and prioritized prefill slots.

Background: Current microbatch shaping reduces pad tokens by bucketing by length, but small tail requests still cause fragmentation and suboptimal kernel selection (underutilized matmul shapes, cache inefficiencies). Prior work (ENG-20377, ENG-54109) improved pad-elision and prefill-aware packing; this design extends that by introducing a short-lived aggregation layer that can be safely undone at decode time and that interacts with KV cache and attention fusion hints.

Proposal highlights: 
- Fragment model: treat sequences < N tokens as fragments; coalescer groups fragments into a virtual batch sequence up to a target combined length or shape conducive to preferred kernels (e.g., matmul-friendly multiples, attention tile sizes). Each fragment retains metadata (original request id, requested output length, soft priority).
- Kernel hinting: annotate virtual batches with kernel-selection hints (fused attention, unpadded-attn path, quantized-kernel) based on combined seqlen and hardware profile. Runtime consults compiled kernel table to pick the best kernel for the virtual batch.
- Prefill priority slots: short fragments frequently arrive as prefill-only requests or as prefill+decode. The scheduler reserves prefill-priority windows to pack fragments first, then interleaves decodes for latency-sensitive fragments to avoid tail latency spikes.
- Decode interleave: at decode time we peel fragments and run token decoding per-request in prioritized order; we support cooperative KV cache boundaries so the prefill packing does not leak context between requests.
- Safety: fragments are strictly isolated logically; no cross-request token mixing. If a request requests streaming or function-calling, it is excluded from coalescing.

Success criteria (metrics): 
- Pad token reduction: >= 35% reduction for tail requests vs baseline bucketing on our e2e benchmark. 
- Throughput: +8–20% token/sec on rtx-8000-equivalent GPU shapes for mixed seqlen traces. 
- Latency: 95p latency regression <= 5% for latency-sensitive classes (we will use decode interleave and prefill-priority to enforce). 
- Regression tests: zero functional regressions across chat, structured-output, and streaming tests.

Work plan / milestones: 
1) Design doc and kernel hint API (this ticket) — design reviewed.
2) Instrumentation PR: collect seqlen histograms and kernel throughput matrix. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/12345)
3) Coalescer prototype: in-memory scheduler + unit tests, synthetic microbench harness.
4) Integrate kernel hinting layer with kernel selector and autoselect heuristics.
5) End-to-end perf tests on staging fleet, tune thresholds and prefill window sizes.
6) Gradual rollout using rollout policy: 10% -> 40% -> 100% with automatic rollback on error or latency regression.

Design trade-offs and notes: 
- Coalescing increases implementation complexity (metadata bookkeeping, KV cache boundaries) but yields better kernel shapes and reduced pad.
- We choose soft-priorities to avoid latency amplification: very latency-sensitive requests bypass coalescing.
- Kernel hinting is advisory; final selection still validated by the kernel selector to avoid poor choices on rare hardware combos.
- We avoid merging requests requiring streaming, function-calls, or explicit deterministic order.

Risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: increased tail latency due to waiting for fragment fill. Mitigation: prefill-priority windows with max wait time and decode interleave; fallback to direct scheduling if wait crosses threshold.
- Risk: bugs leaking context across fragments. Mitigation: strict KV-scoped boundaries, end-to-end privacy tests, and fuzzer tests.

Artifacts and links: 
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RUNTIME/Fragment+Coalescer+Design 
- Perf dashboard (staging): https://grafana.redwood.com/d/frag-coalescer/staging-perf
- Prototype PR (instrumentation): https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/12345
- Prototype coalescer branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/compare/feature/fragment-coalescer

Rollout plan: start in dedicated staging pool with synthetic traces; enable feature flag off by default. Canary to 10% real traffic for 48h, monitor token/sec, 95p latency, error rates, and pad tokens. If regressions exceed thresholds (95p latency +5%, error rate +0.1%), rollback and tune parameters.
